name: Orgrim Doomhammer
summary: During the Second War, Orgrim Doomhammer led the Old Horde as its supreme Warchief. He became one of history’s greatest orc warriors. He died freeing the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, but his legacy lives on in Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his warhammer and black plate armor.

sections.title: Rise of the Warchief
sections.body:
Orgrim Doomhammer rose from second-in-command to become Chieftain of the Blackrock clan. Gul'dan offered him demonic blood, but Orgrim refused and kept his doubts hidden beneath fierce loyalty. Near the end of the First War, he turned against the Shadow Council after its treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan.

Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat and took the mantle of Warchief. He purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. A devastating strategist, he drove human kingdoms to the brink of ruin. Gul'dan's betrayal split his forces, and Orgrim was defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire.

sections.title: Fall and Legacy
sections.body:
Orgrim Doomhammer escaped human captivity and lived in hiding until he met Thrall, Durotan's orphaned son. The young shaman's vision gave Orgrim new purpose, and he rallied the remaining orcish clans to storm the internment camps and free their people.

During a fierce battle at an encampment in the Arathi Highlands, a lance struck the Warchief from behind. As he lay dying, Orgrim gave Thrall his black plate armor, his ancestral weapon, the Doomhammer, and the title of Warchief. The liberated outpost was renamed Hammerfall in his honor, and the newly founded capital in Durotar was named Orgrimmar.

faq.answer: Orgrim Doomhammer was Chieftain of the Blackrock clan and Warchief of the Horde during the Second War. After escaping human captivity, he fought beside Thrall to free their imprisoned kin and died in the Arathi Highlands.

Orgrim Doomhammer was struck from behind by a knight's lance during an assault on a human internment camp in the Arathi Highlands. Thrall took up his mantle, and the site was named Hammerfall in his memory.

faq.q: Why is the Horde capital named Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Thrall named the fortified city in Durotar for Orgrim Doomhammer, his mentor and predecessor. Orgrim saw promise in Thrall and named him the new Warchief, so the Horde could rebuild on honor rather than demonic corruption.

faq.q: Did Orgrim drink the demon blood?
faq.answer: No. Orgrim Doomhammer refused the demonic blood and concealed his doubts behind loyalty to Blackhand. He later destroyed Gul'dan's Shadow Council from within.

angles.text: As an orc, you revere Orgrim Doomhammer for freeing your people from lethargy and internment. He chose honor over demonic subjugation.
To the Alliance, Orgrim Doomhammer remains a grim symbol of how close the Eastern Kingdoms came to ruin during the Second War. He butchered countless champions before his defeat at Blackrock Spire.
